label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 13
knowledgePattern: Test global order equivalence for roots, powers and reciprocals
solution:
The real fifth-root function is strictly increasing on all real numbers: x<y if and only if x1/5<y1/5. Thus G has both required implication directions.

A reverses the reciprocal-cube-root inequality correctly only within a same-sign interval; it fails for x = −1, y = 1. B reverses the increasing fifth-root order. C and E lose sign information, as x = −8, y = −1 shows. D fails at x = 1, y = 8. F also fails for these positive inputs because reciprocals reverse their order.

The nonzero domain permits all these examples and does not prevent opposite signs. Answer G.

hints.title: Test across every sign region
hints.body: Check each transformation on negative inputs, positive inputs and a pair straddling zero.
hints.recap: Inequality transformations must be justified on the whole stated domain.
hints.pitfall: Excluding zero does not require the two inputs to have the same sign.
hints.pause: Look for an admissible pair that invalidates each doubtful equivalence.

recall.reminder: Inequality transformations must be justified on the whole stated domain.

hints.title: Check both directions for the survivor
hints.body: For any remaining transformation, determine whether distinct inputs retain their strict order and whether the transformation can collapse two different inputs.
hints.recap: Necessary and sufficient requires both implications, not just a few successful examples.
hints.pitfall: Even powers and absolute values can discard sign information.
hints.pause: Give a general order argument before choosing the option.
